title: Continuous batching horizon calibrator with KV backpressure controls for mixed prompt/response workloads
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Problem statement:

Our continuous batching scheduler under mixed prompt/response workloads shows unstable tail latency and suboptimal GPU memory utilization. Short prompts followed by long decodes create uneven slot residency and cause KV cache churn: frequent small sessions pin and evict KV pages needed for longer decodes, increasing CPU/GPU memcpy and degrading p95/p99. Existing heuristics (fixed tenure, static watermarking) are brittle across tenants with different prompt/response distributions.

Goal:

Design and implement a Horizon Calibrator layer in the continuous batcher that: 1) dynamically adjusts coalescing horizons (how long a slot waits to be coalesced into a batch) per-length stratum, 2) applies KV backpressure and soft-reservations to prevent short-lived traffic from evicting warm KV entries needed by long decodes, and 3) coordinates with GPU slab allocator to reduce fragmentation during mixed-length workloads.

Non-goals:

- Changing model kernels/quantization strategies (handled by separate teams).
- Large infra changes to allocator APIs beyond exposing a small advise()/pin() surface.

Design overview:

1) Length strata and micro-horizons
- Classify requests into length strata at enqueue time: short (<=64 tokens), medium (65-512), long (>512). Buckets are tunable and sampled per tenant.
- Maintain an exponentially-weighted moving average (EWMA) of observed decode times per stratum and a per-stratum horizon H_s = alpha * median_decode + beta * median_enqueue_gap. H_s is clamped to [min_horizon, max_horizon].

2) Horizon-driven coalescing
- Batcher defers slot sealing for up to H_s (per-slot) to allow more compatible tokens to join. Short-stratum slots get smaller H_s; long-stratum slots get larger H_s to maximize KV residency reuse during multi-token decodes.

3) KV backpressure and soft-reservations
- Introduce per-GPU KV reservation scoreboard: a quota of KV pages reserved for active long decodes (configurable percent of total KV capacity). When reservations approach threshold, allow the batcher to apply backpressure for short-stratum requests (prefer tail-latency-shedding or route to a lower-cost model variant).
- Provide an allocator hint API: advise_reserve(gpu_id, pages) and release_reserve(...). Long-decode leaders call advise_reserve at start-of-decode; reservation is released on decode completion or graceful fallback.

4) GPU slab alignment and compaction hints
- Coordinate with GPU slab allocator to prefer slab-aligned KV objects for long-lived entries. Periodic off-peak compaction API can be invoked to defragment KV memory when utilization crosses a fragmentation threshold.

5) Telemetry and adaptive control loop
- Telemetry signals: per-stratum enqueue rate, slot coalescing ratio, per-stratum decode latency EWMA, KV hit/miss rates, KV eviction churn, slab fragmentation percent, GPU memcpy/sec, and token-per-second throughput.
- A control loop evaluates these signals every evaluation window (default 15s) and adjusts H_s, reservation percent, and backpressure thresholds using hill-climbing with safety clamps.

Success metrics (measured against a representative mixed-traffic benchmark):
- p95 latency for decode phase <= baseline p95 + 10ms (goal: reduce p99 by 20%).
- KV eviction churn reduced by >= 35%.
- GPU memcpy volume reduced by >= 25% during mixed workloads.
- End-to-end throughput (tokens/sec) >= baseline or improved by >5% in long-decode heavy mixes.
- No >2x increase in short-request p50 latency; any short-request degradation must be controlled via customer-tier policies.

Compatibility & rollout policy:

- Feature gated behind runtime flag: continuous.horizon_calibrator (defaults off).
- Canary rollout: 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 2 weeks with automatic rollback on SLO breach.
- Per-tenant opt-out and soft-reservation tuning exposed in Dedicated/Private configs.

Testing plan:

1) Unit tests for horizon math, EWMA, and clamp logic.
2) Integration tests in CI: synthetic traffic generator with controlled mixes (short-only, long-only, mixed 70/30 & 30/70) verifying telemetry and control adjustments.
3) Staging: traffic-replay tests with customer traces that historically caused KV churn. Compare baseline vs calibrator behavior with trace replay.
4) Performance bench: run GPU microbench with slab instrumentation to measure memcpy/sec and fragmentation before/after.

Instrumentation and dashboards:

- New metrics: horizon_ms_by_stratum, kv_reserved_pages, kv_evictions_by_cause, slab_fragmentation_pct, slot_seal_delay_ms, coalesce_ratio_by_stratum.
- Dashboards: Continuous Batcher -> Horizon Calibrator (per-gpu, per-tenant filters).
- Alerts: sustained kv_evictions_by_cause > threshold for 60s, slab_fragmentation_pct > 70% for 5m, or p99 decode latency drift > 25% vs baseline.

Rollout steps and fallback:

- Step 0: Merge feature as disabled. Add comprehensive unit/integration tests.
- Step 1: Internal QA with synthetic mixes and bench runs.
- Step 2: Canary 0.5% on low-risk tenants. Monitor tuned metrics for 24h.
- Step 3: If KV eviction decreases and p99 improves, expand to 10% and then to 50%. If regressions occur, automatically revert the flag and capture heap profile + KV metrics.
- Emergency fallback: disable continuous.horizon_calibrator and optionally set reservation percent to 0 to restore prior behavior.

Open questions / trade-offs:

- How aggressive should soft-reservations be for multi-tenant GPUs? Too aggressive risks starving short interactive traffic; too conservative yields little benefit. Proposed default: reserve 18% pages for long decodes, tunable by tenant.
- Reservation accounting: should reservations be token-count based or page-count based? Page-count is simpler with current allocator metrics; token-based would need mapping of KV size per token distribution.
- Do we allow cross-GPU spill reservations for dedicated customers? (later PR if requested).

Dependencies and follow-ups:

- Allocator API: expose advise_reserve/release_reserve (ENG-914321).
- Runtime telemetry: slab fragmentation instrumentation (ENG-842100).
- Policy UI: expose per-tenant reservation tuning in Console (PM follow-up).

Acceptance criteria:

- Implementation merged behind feature flag with tests.
- Bench results demonstrate >= 25% reduction in GPU memcpy/sec and >= 30% reduction in KV eviction churn for mixed workloads in staging.
- Canary run shows no SLO regression for short-request p95 beyond agreed thresholds and p99 decode improvements for long requests.
- Documentation and dashboard tiles published in Console release notes.
